text:
Fedor Svechkov is learning a new team on a short leash. After 122 games in Nashville, the 23-year-old has 8 points in 21 games for Colorado, but his ice time has drifted down to about 10 minutes a night over his last ten, and in eight of those ten games he didn't register a shot on goal. His Saturday winner in Montreal, a drive to the net, was his first goal in that stretch.

The skating is real: his top speed sits in the 99th percentile in NHL Edge tracking. So is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 83rd percentile for primary shot assists last season, and his plays-like matches lean the same way, more passer than finisher. What isn't real yet is the scoring rate. He's shooting 20% against a likely range closer to 12%, and the Avalanche have created less with him on the ice than without him at five on five.

Watch his minutes. A fourth-line passer with elite speed needs linemates who shoot.
